network.confirmed_means: the citation's own title words were found on the fetched page. A bare HTTP 200 is never enough.

not_covered.why: No entity extraction is implemented. Recognising 'Frank Darvall' as a person and checking that the person said the thing needs either a gazetteer or a model, and guessing from capitalisation would produce confident nonsense.
Requires an archive pass that is not built. Every archive hop is recorded BROKEN.
Detected but never adjudicated. A connective word is not a causal claim and no automated verdict is offered.
Attributions are located, but whether the quoted words match the source text is not checked. That needs the source, which needs network.
Table numbers live in prose, not in markup. Nothing binds 'Table 2' to a specific table block, so these resolve only to a plausible range.

not_covered.kind: external source content, beyond the title
not_covered.why: The network half fetched every Works Cited URL and asked whether the citation's own title words appear on the page, which is why a bare 200 is never enough to confirm one. It does NOT read the source and check that it supports the sentence citing it. A LIVE_CONFIRMED citation is a real page carrying the right title, not a verified argument. PDFs are fetched but never parsed, so they stay unconfirmed on purpose.
